root_idea.summary: The root centers on whiteness or hoariness, especially white hair and the appearance of white among what was dark.
root_idea.development: The lexical development extends from gray or white hair and the onset of aging to hair or heads becoming white, mountains whitened by snow or frost, and winter months named for the whiteness of the earth. A proposed root-level connection with intermixture is reflected in white strands appearing among dark hair.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized noun شَيْب.
شَيْبَة is a related verbal-noun variant for whiteness or hoariness of the hair and is grouped with شَيْب.
The Quranic plural شِيب is presented under its supported adjective citation form أَشْيَب.

senses.definition: White or gray hair; whiteness or hoariness of the hair, including the onset or spread of grayness.
senses.usage_conditions: The related form شَيْبَة functions as a verbal-noun or noun variant in the same lexical branch. In وَاشْتَعَلَ الرَّأْسُ شَيْبًا, شَيْبًا specifies the whiteness spreading through the head, or is understood as an infinitive describing that process.

senses.definition: White-haired or hoary ones; the plural substantive of أَشْيَب.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence is the plural form شِيب, used substantively for those characterized by white or gray hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become white-haired or hoary; of the head or hair, to become white.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may be intransitive of a person or head, and may also be used transitively with the head as object, meaning to whiten the head. The hills may likewise be described as becoming white or hoary by extension.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone or the head to become white-haired or hoary.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative use, including the construction in which grief makes a person or his head hoary.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have children who have become white-haired or hoary.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a man whose children have reached that condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The thong at the upper extremity of a whip.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A whip is said to have two such thongs, شِيبَانِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An imitative word for the sound made by camels’ lips while drinking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An onomatopoeic use distinct from the gray-hair noun and plural adjective.
A reported conventional or postclassical specialization of the headword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name for certain artemisia plants and lichens.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The botanical references include artemisia arborescens, lichen prunastri, and شَيْبَةُ الجَبَلِ, a lichen designation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The two coldest winter months, the two months of قِمَاح.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is explained by the whiteness of the earth under frost or snow; شِيبَان alone can also designate the first of these months.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Snow- or frost-whitened mountains; by extension, white clouds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may describe mountains white with snow, hoarfrost, or dust, and some usage applies it to white clouds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of truffles, white; in one description, white and large.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive use applied to truffles.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A day marked by cold and cloud.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In يَوْمٌ أَشْيَبُ, the clouds are described as thin or cold, humid clouds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The last night of the lunar month.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression contrasts with the first night, called لَيْلَةُ حُرَّةٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an idiom concerning a woman, the night on which she is deflowered.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This idiomatic use is contrasted with بِلَيْلَةِ حُرَّةٍ, said when she has not been deflowered.

cautions: شَيْبَة is grouped with شَيْب for the Quranic gray-hair sense, while its separately reported white-or-hoary-beard specialization is kept among broader Classical meanings.
The phrase لَيْلَةُ شَيْبَاءَ has two distinct reported uses in the evidence: the last night of the lunar month and an idiom for defloration.
The spelling شِيب has unrelated Classical uses for a whip thong and an imitative camel-drinking sound; the Quranic occurrence is the plural substantive of أَشْيَب.
